prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2010 manifesto is a call to restore British self-government by leaving the undemocratic EU superstate, reclaiming sovereignty, and ending crippling Brussels regulation and costs. The party argues departure delivers three freedoms: action (Britain sets its own policy and trade deals), resources (billions saved from EU fees and red tape), and people (power back to Westminster and voters through binding referenda). UKIP rejects the LibLabCon consensus for surrendering powers and breaking referendum promises.

Core economic plan
- Simpler, lower taxes: raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a single 31% flat tax (merging income tax and employee NI) starting at that threshold; phase out employers’ NI; abolish inheritance tax when feasible.
- Slash waste, quangos, and politically correct non-jobs; restore the state to its 1997 size while protecting frontline services.
- Replace EU VAT with a Local Sales Tax, share business rates with councils, and cut council tax by scrapping costly EU mandates.
- Restore Bank of England authority; split retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall style); raise capital ratios.

Jobs, industry, skills
- Rebuild a productive economy via long-term programs: defence procurement, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport upgrades, and prison building—driving around one million skilled jobs.
- Create Production Enterprise Centres for SME innovation; denationalise universities/FE via student and training vouchers; curb predatory foreign takeovers in strategic sectors; scrap EU green levies that hinder firms.

Immigration and asylum
- End mass, uncontrolled immigration with a five-year freeze on permanent settlement; strictly controlled, Australian-style points system thereafter; regain border control by leaving the EU.
- No amnesty for illegal immigrants; enforce removals; repeal the Human Rights Act and exit the ECHR to restore parliamentary supremacy.

Law and order
- Victims first, zero tolerance: elected Police Boards; life means life; double prison capacity; three-strikes for persistent offenders; restore homeowners’ rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant.

Defence
- Increase spending by 40%; expand the Army and Reserves; rebuild the Navy (including three carriers); strengthen the RAF; keep and renew an independent nuclear deterrent; NATO first, not EU defence.

NHS and care
- No cuts to frontline care; slash bureaucracy; elected County Health Boards; franchise services to drive efficiency while assets stay public; health credit vouchers for those choosing private cover; restore matrons and on-the-job nurse training; free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education
- Parental choice via school vouchers; protect and expand grammar/professional schools; rigorous basics; teacher training on the job; end 50% university target; restore merit; franchise schools; elected County Education Boards.

Pensions and welfare
- Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week, non-means-tested; restore dividend tax credit; rein in unaffordable public sector pensions.
- Replace 70+ benefits with a Basic Cash Benefit; make work pay up to the higher personal allowance; rationalise child and nursery support; require workfare for some recipients; restrict benefits to citizens/residents of five years.

Foreign policy and trade
- Leave the EU for a Swiss-style free trade deal; reclaim the UK seat at the WTO; champion a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; pursue global trade pacts; back democracy worldwide.

Energy and environment
- Expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; support domestic coal with cleaner plants; oppose uneconomic wind, keep large schemes offshore; repeal the Climate Change Act and EU energy directives; invest in flood defences and practical environmental improvements.

Transport
- Invest £3bn more per year: better roads, three high-speed rail lines, reopen routes, shift freight to rail/canals; Britdisc for foreign lorries; fair fuel policy; oppose Heathrow expansion in favour of a Thames Estuary hub.

Housing and planning
- Control demand by controlling immigration; empower communities with binding local referenda; scrap regional quangos and hidden development taxes; protect Green Belt via elected conservators.

Constitution and governance
- Direct democracy: binding referenda by citizen petition; AV+ electoral reform; recall powers; abolish regional government; English Parliament days; strengthen Parliament’s war/treaty powers; support the monarchy and Church settlement.

Culture and Britishness
- Civic nationalism, not multiculturalism: merit over quotas; protect iconic measures and institutions; teach Britain’s contributions; confront extremist Islam (including burqa/niqab bans in specified settings and deporting violent preachers); celebrate the Commonwealth and St George’s Day.

Farming and countryside
- Leave the CAP but avoid sudden subsidy losses; pro-consumer labelling; reform harmful EU directives; empower producer co-ops; supermarket ombudsman; local referenda on hunting.

Fishing
- Exit the CFP; reclaim waters (200-mile EEZ); end discards and industrial fishing; rebuild stocks with enforceable management.

Other
- Protect animal welfare; safeguard Royal Mail and Post Offices; allow designated smoking rooms; champion small business.
